910.name: Prehistoric & Roman Emona
910.description: The Slovenian lands harbour extraordinary prehistoric sites, including the world's oldest known wooden wheel. Roman Emona (Ljubljana) and Poetovio (Ptuj) became important frontier cities of the empire.

sub_clusters.name: Prehistoric Settlements & Pile Dwellings
sub_clusters.description: The Ljubljana Marshes pile dwellings (UNESCO), the world's oldest wooden wheel (c. 3200 BCE), Hallstatt culture, Celtic Taurisci and Norican Kingdom.
key_events: Ljubljana Marshes wooden wheel crafted – oldest in the world (c. 3200 BCE)

sub_clusters.name: Roman Emona & Poetovio
sub_clusters.description: Roman conquest of the Norican and Pannonian territories, the founding of Emona (Ljubljana) and Poetovio (Ptuj) as legionary centres, and the region's role on the empire's Danubian frontier.

920.name: Carantania & Frankish Integration
920.description: The Slavic principality of Carantania (c. 630–828) was one of the earliest Slavic states. Its unique installation ritual of dukes influenced political philosophy. Christianisation and Frankish/Bavarian overlordship gradually absorbed Carantanian autonomy.

sub_clusters.name: Principality of Carantania
sub_clusters.description: The formation of Carantania under Duke Valuk, the unique ducal installation ceremony at the Prince's Stone (Knežji kamen), and the Christianisation mission of Bishop Virgil of Salzburg.
key_events: Carantania – one of the earliest Slavic polities – established (c. 630)

sub_clusters.name: Frankish Overlordship & Christianisation
sub_clusters.description: Loss of Carantanian autonomy under Frankish rule, the Liudewit revolt (819–823), full Christianisation, and the Freising Manuscripts (c. 972–1039) – the oldest known Slavic text in Latin script.

920.name: Medieval Slovenian Lands under the HRE
920.description: The Slovenian lands were divided among Carniola, Styria, Carinthia, and Gorizia within the Holy Roman Empire. Despite political fragmentation, a distinct Slovenian-speaking identity persisted through peasant communities and local church traditions.

sub_clusters.name: Duchies of Carniola, Styria & Carinthia
sub_clusters.description: The Slovenian lands as marches and duchies of the HRE, the counts of Celje's rise, and the region's role in the empire's southeastern frontier.

sub_clusters.name: Habsburg Acquisition & Counts of Celje
sub_clusters.description: Habsburg consolidation of the Slovenian lands (Carniola from 1335), the powerful Counts of Celje as rivals, and the great peasant revolts of the 15th century against feudal burdens and Ottoman raids.

930.name: Reformation & Habsburg Absolutism
930.description: The Protestant Reformation under Primož Trubar created the first Slovenian books and codified the literary language. Habsburg Counter-Reformation crushed Protestantism, but the linguistic legacy endured. Ottoman raids shaped the frontier experience.

sub_clusters.name: Primož Trubar & the Slovenian Reformation
sub_clusters.description: Primož Trubar's 'Catechismus' and 'Abecedarium' (1550) as the first printed books in Slovenian, Jurij Dalmatin's Bible translation (1584), and the development of Slovenian as a literary language.
key_events: Primož Trubar publishes the first Slovenian book – Catechismus (1550)
Jurij Dalmatin publishes the complete Bible in Slovenian (1584)

sub_clusters.name: Counter-Reformation & Ottoman Frontier
sub_clusters.description: Habsburg Counter-Reformation suppressing Protestantism, the Military Frontier system against Ottoman incursions, and the Enlightenment-era reforms of Maria Theresa and Joseph II.

940.name: Illyrian Provinces & National Awakening
940.description: Napoleon's Illyrian Provinces (1809–13) briefly introduced modern administration and elevated Slovenian as a language of instruction. This spark fuelled the 19th-century national awakening, with the 'United Slovenia' programme demanding a unified Slovenian-speaking crownland.

sub_clusters.name: Napoleonic Illyrian Provinces
sub_clusters.description: Napoleon's creation of the Illyrian Provinces with Ljubljana as capital, the elevation of Slovenian in schools and administration, and the lasting impact on national consciousness.
key_events: Napoleon establishes the Illyrian Provinces with capital at Ljubljana (1809)

sub_clusters.name: Spring of Nations & 'United Slovenia'
sub_clusters.description: The 1848 'United Slovenia' (Zedinjena Slovenija) programme demanding unification of Slovenian lands, France Prešeren's poetry and the national anthem, and the Slovenian political awakening within Austria-Hungary.

950.name: World Wars & Yugoslav Slovenia
950.description: Slovenians fought on the Isonzo Front in WWI, then joined the Kingdom of Serbs, Croats and Slovenes. WWII saw tripartite occupation (German, Italian, Hungarian) and a powerful Partisan resistance movement.

sub_clusters.name: WWI – Isonzo Front
sub_clusters.description: The devastating twelve Battles of the Isonzo fought on Slovenian soil, the Caporetto breakthrough (1917), and Slovenian soldiers serving in the Austro-Hungarian army.

sub_clusters.name: Interwar Yugoslavia & WWII Tripartite Occupation
sub_clusters.description: Slovenians in the Kingdom of Yugoslavia, the loss of the Primorska region to Italy, WWII tripartite occupation and Nazi Germanisation, and the Partisan liberation struggle.
key_events: Liberation Front of the Slovenian People formed (27 April 1941)

950.name: SR Slovenia in Socialist Yugoslavia
950.description: Slovenia was the most economically developed Yugoslav republic. Its relative liberalism, strong industrial base, and opening to the West made it the first republic to push for democratisation and sovereignty.

sub_clusters.name: Socialist Modernisation & Economic Leadership
sub_clusters.description: Slovenia's rapid industrialisation, highest GDP per capita in Yugoslavia, cultural liberalisation, and the development of a distinct Slovenian civil society.

sub_clusters.name: Democratisation & JBTZ Trial
sub_clusters.description: The JBTZ affair (1988) galvanising Slovenian opposition, the 'Slovenian Spring,' multi-party elections (1990), and the plebiscite on independence (88.5% in favour, 23 December 1990).
key_events: Slovenian independence plebiscite – 88.5% vote yes (23 Dec 1990)

960.name: Ten-Day War & Independence
960.description: Slovenia declared independence on 25 June 1991, triggering a brief Ten-Day War with the Yugoslav People's Army. International recognition followed, and Slovenia rapidly transitioned to a market economy and democratic governance.

sub_clusters.name: Ten-Day War (1991)
sub_clusters.description: Slovenia's declaration of independence (25 June 1991), the brief Ten-Day War with JNA forces, the Brioni Accord brokered by the EC, and international recognition.
key_events: Slovenia declares independence; Ten-Day War begins (25 June 1991)

sub_clusters.name: Democratic Transition & EU Preparations
sub_clusters.description: Economic transition, privatisation, constitutional development under Milan Kučan's presidency, and the accession negotiations for EU and NATO membership.

960.name: EU & Euro Integration
960.description: Slovenia joined the EU and NATO in 2004, adopted the euro in 2007 (first post-communist state to do so), held the EU Council presidency in 2008 and 2021, and established itself as a stable Central European democracy.

sub_clusters.name: EU & NATO Accession (2004)
sub_clusters.description: Slovenia's accession to the EU and NATO on 1 May 2004, Schengen area entry (2007), and the adoption of the euro on 1 January 2007 – the first former Yugoslav and post-communist state to do so.
key_events: Slovenia joins the EU and NATO (1 May 2004)
Slovenia adopts the euro – first post-communist state (1 Jan 2007)

sub_clusters.name: Modern Slovenia & EU Presidencies
sub_clusters.description: Slovenia's two EU Council presidencies (2008, 2021), navigating the 2008 financial crisis, the border dispute with Croatia (resolved at The Hague), and contemporary political developments.

unassigned_events.note: Events not yet assigned to a thematic cluster
